title: Air India Board Convenes in Mumbai as New CEO Gebremariam Prepares to Take Charge
excerpt: Directors led by N. Chandrasekaran met at Bombay House to set the pay package for incoming chief Tewolde Gebremariam and formalize the handover from outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson.
body:
• Air India's board met at Bombay House in Mumbai on Tuesday, September 15, with the pay package for incoming CEO and MD Tewolde Gebremariam on the agenda, according to sources cited by PTI.
  • The meeting marks the formal handover as Campbell Wilson steps down this month after leading the Tata-owned carrier's transformation since July 2022.
  • Wilson's own package — up to ₹27.75 crore with roughly 60% tied to performance — was approved in May 2025, a fortnight before the fatal AI171 crash that killed 260 people.
  • The incoming chief inherits a loss-making airline under pressure from airspace closures, fuel costs, operational disruptions and heightened scrutiny of safety.

Air India's board of directors convened in Mumbai on Tuesday, September 15, to discuss the compensation package for incoming chief executive Tewolde Gebremariam and formally begin the handover from Campbell Wilson, who steps down this month, according to sources cited by PTI.

The meeting was chaired by Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekaran at Bombay House, the group's Mumbai headquarters. Chandrasekaran, Wilson and Gebremariam were seen arriving together ahead of the session. The seven-member board also includes independent directors Sanjiv Mehta, Alice G. Vaidyan and P.R. Ramesh, and non-executive, non-independent directors P.B. Balaji and Goh Choon Phong.

Directors are expected to formally thank Wilson for his tenure. Speaking to reporters outside the venue, Wilson described his time at the airline and in India as "a wonderful experience."

Context & Background

Wilson took charge in July 2022, six months after the Tata Group reclaimed Air India from the government in January 2022; Singapore Airlines later acquired a 25.1% stake. He inherited an airline with an aging fleet, operational strains and a balance sheet deep in the red, and oversaw the first phase of the group's ambitious Vihaan.AI transformation.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2099791170591134002

The incoming CEO is not a novice in turnarounds. Tewolde Gebremariam previously ran Ethiopian Airlines, where he oversaw rapid expansion of the carrier's fleet, network and revenues and helped build Addis Ababa into a major international hub, according to earlier Mint reporting — a track record that appears to be the main reason Tata tapped him.

On September 7, Gebremariam addressed Air India staff for the first time at a town hall, asking for their support and cooperation, urging them to minimize disruptions, and stressing that operational excellence is about getting the basics right every day. Chandrasekaran used the same occasion to emphasize safety and a stronger culture of cost consciousness.

"We will Make Air India Great Again (MAGA)."

— Tewolde Gebremariam, incoming CEO and MD, Air India

His inheritance is formidable. The loss-making airline is still dealing with the fallout of the AI171 crash in Ahmedabad in June 2025, which killed 260 people — one of India's worst aviation disasters — on top of geopolitical disruptions, airspace closures, fuel-price volatility and repeated operational issues.

Pay itself is a sensitive signal. In May 2025, the board approved a package for Wilson worth up to ₹27.75 crore: ₹11.1 crore in fixed salary, ₹8.32 crore in performance-linked bonuses and ₹8.32 crore in long-term stock incentives — a 46% jump over his ₹18.98 crore earnings in 2023-24, according to Mint. The approval came a fortnight before the AI171 crash, and about 60% of his pay was tied to the airline's performance.

Impact & Analysis

Setting Gebremariam's pay structure is the board's first public measure of how Tata values the turnaround task — and how much performance risk it wants the new chief to carry. Given the scrutiny around Wilson's raise just before AI171, a package weighted more toward safety and reliability metrics than raw growth would read as a deliberate correction.

The transition also tests continuity. Air India is mid-fleet-renewal, with more than 100 aircraft expected to join the group in 2027 and 2028, and every schedule disruption now lands harder with regulators, passengers and courts than it did two years ago.

Diaspora Angle

Air India remains the default carrier for many NRIs on India routes, including to US and UK gateways, so a stable leadership handover and a chief visibly accountable for safety and on-time performance matter directly to diaspora flyers choosing the airline for family travel.

What's Next / Looking Ahead

Gebremariam formally takes charge later this month. Watch for the board-approved pay structure, any executive-team reshuffle, and the new chief's first moves on operational reliability and fleet induction.
